summary.text: A male mixed-breed kitten, approximately 2 months old and weighing 300 g, rescued from the streets, was referred to a veterinary ophthalmology service after ocular alterations had been empirically treated as chronic bilateral conjunctivitis without response, using several eye drops and ointments per the caregiver. Examination showed intense bilateral conjunctival hyperemia, granulomatous appearance, follicles, chemosis, thick mucopurulent discharge and malnutrition, without cutaneous lesions.

After a 5-day washout, FIV and FeLV tests were negative, the blood count showed no significant changes and conjunctival scraping showed inflammatory cells without fungal structures. Empirical acyclovir for 5 days was followed by gentamicin drops after the antibiogram identified Enterococcus sp. The owner then used gentamicin with dexamethasone drops and systemic corticosteroids, and 15 days later the condition had worsened and a limb ulcer appeared.

Aspirate cytology of the conjunctivae and the skin lesion showed yeasts consistent with Sporothrix spp., and fungal culture and microscopy supported sporotrichosis. Itraconazole 10 mg/kg with SAMe was started, adjusted to 50 mg/animal after 35 days with only slight regression, and a topical itraconazole 2% and beta-glucan lotion was then added, with improvement after 10 days and clinical resolution after 30 days.

Therapy was extended by 30 days to 4 months and 5 days in total, with clinical remission after 4 months. At the end of therapy bilateral symblepharon and eyelid fibrosis were present, and surgical correction was indicated for the symblepharon.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says that after 1 month of therapy the lesions disappeared, leaving the only sequelae as adhesion of the third eyelid to the palpebral conjunctiva. The case text reports clinical resolution 30 days after the topical lotion, remission after 4 months of treatment, and bilateral symblepharon plus eyelid fibrosis at the end of therapy.

evidence.quote: After 1 month of therapy, the lesions disappeared, leaving the only sequelae as adhesion of the third eyelid to the palpebral conjunctiva.
At the end of the therapy, bilateral symblepharon was observed, for which surgical correction was indicated; and eyelid fibrosis as a consequence of intense conjunctival inflammation (Figure 5C).

ambiguities.must_not_infer: That the abstract 1 month refers to the topical lotion or any specific start point, or that adhesion of the third eyelid is the same finding as symblepharon.

figures.caption_summary: Cytological image from a sample obtained from the ocular conjunctiva by fine-needle aspiration, stained with a rapid Romanowsky-type stain. A pyogranulomatous inflammatory infiltrate is evident, composed of numerous degenerated neutrophils and macrophages. Rounded, sometimes ovoid to fusiform (“cigar-shaped”) yeast-like structures, surrounded by a thin clear halo and with a basophilic center, compatible with Sporothrix spp., are observed (arrows). Tissue architecture is not preserved, consistent with exfoliative material. Magnification: 1000 × .
